description: Introduces the rich indigenous scientific heritage of India, covering ancient mathematics, Paninian computational linguistics, logical epistemology, and sustainable philosophy.
learning_objectives: Appreciate the historical evolution of scientific and philosophical thought in India.
Understand mathematical and astronomical contributions of Aryabhata, Brahmagupta, and the Kerala School.
Explore Ashtadhyayi as a formal computational generative grammar and knowledge representation system.
Analyze Nyaya logical inquiry, debate systems, and ethical governance frameworks.
outline: Indian Knowledge Traditions: Epistemology, historical timeline, classification of Vedic and classical scientific corpus.
Mathematics & Astronomy: Sulba Sutras, binary systems in Pingala, Aryabhatiya, Brahmagupta's zero and algebra, Madhava's infinite series.
Computational Linguistics & Paninian Grammar: Panini's Ashtadhyayi formal grammar, morphological rules, Sanskrit as a computing language structure.
Logic & Scientific Inquiry: Nyaya-Vaisheshika epistemology, 16 categories of logic, Anumana (inference), debate frameworks (Vada/Jalpa/Vitanda).
Ethics, Governance & Sustainable Science: Arthashastra statecraft, ecological philosophy in traditional water management, Ayurveda holistic health principles.
